checkpoint.title: NEON_OAM: DeepForest NEON tree-crown RetinaNet fine-tuned on OAM Freetown chips. Its ResNet-50 initialises the U-Net encoder; the decoder starts untrained

properties.title: Segment tree crowns
properties.description: U-Net tree-crown segmenter: a ResNet-50 encoder taken from the DeepForest NEON_OAM detector, with a U-Net decoder trained on OAM chips of Freetown and OSM tree labels (polygons, and tree points turned into crown discs). It predicts the tree canopy of each chip as a probability map and returns one polygon per canopy patch in EPSG:4326, holes included. Inference scales each chip to the model's resolution from the zoom and row in its OAM file name, then runs one ONNX pass; thresholding, polygon tracing and georeferencing run in the pinned ts-hot library. The base checkpoint holds the encoder only, so a decoder must be trained (or a trained U-Net checkpoint supplied) before predictions are meaningful.

properties.mlm:architecture: U-Net (ResNet-50 encoder of DeepForest NEON_OAM, bilinear upsampling decoder)

fair:metrics_spec.name: Pixel Precision
fair:metrics_spec.description: Share of predicted tree pixels that are tree in the labels, summed over the val split at the inference threshold. Labels: polygons, and tree points as crown discs; points without a diameter are ignored.

fair:metrics_spec.name: Pixel Recall
fair:metrics_spec.description: Share of labelled tree pixels that the model predicts as tree, summed over the val split at the inference threshold.

fair:metrics_spec.name: Pixel F1
fair:metrics_spec.description: Harmonic mean of pixel precision and recall over the val split.

fair:metrics_spec.name: Pixel IoU
fair:metrics_spec.description: Intersection over union of the tree class over the val split: intersecting pixels divided by the union of predicted and labelled tree pixels.

mlm:output.name: tree probability
mlm:output.description: ONNX output `probability`: per-pixel probability of tree canopy in model-input pixels, before thresholding.

mlm:output.name: tree canopy
mlm:output.description: Tree canopy polygons after thresholding, tracing, a minimum area and simplification, one polygon per feature, with holes.

label.description: Class name of the predicted class (tree).

confidence.description: Mean probability of the pixels of the polygon.

source.description: File name of the chip the polygon was detected in.

fair:split_spec.description: Spatial block split on OAM-x-y-z tile coords: chips grouped into (x // block_size, y // block_size) blocks, whole blocks assigned to train or val, because neighbouring chips share canopy and trees cut at chip borders. Chips must be named OAM-x-y-z.tif; any other name is rejected. Chips without a label are kept as background examples.

fair:hyperparameters_spec.description: Fine-tuning epochs.
Chips per training batch. Each chip is scaled to the model's resolution (about 3x at zoom 20) before the network, so memory per chip is high.
AdamW learning rate of the trainable weights (the encoder uses encoder_lr_factor times this).
AdamW weight decay.
Share of the chips held out as spatial validation.
Seed for the block order of the spatial split.
Side of a spatial block, in tile units.
Keep the ResNet-50 encoder frozen and train only the decoder. Recommended for small datasets; keeps what the NEON_OAM encoder learned. BatchNorm statistics always stay frozen.
With a frozen encoder, still train the ResNet stages from this one on.
Learning-rate multiplier for the encoder weights that train.
Gradient clipping norm; 0 disables clipping.
cosine decays to 0 over all batches of the run; none keeps the learning rate constant.
Batches of linear learning-rate ramp-up.
Each epoch trains on a fresh random fraction of the chips.
Epochs without a better validation loss before training stops.
Weight of the Dice loss next to the binary cross-entropy; 0 uses cross-entropy only.
Metres of ground per pixel the network sees. Training and inference must use the same value.
Cap on the longest side of a scaled chip, which bounds memory at coarse zooms.
Probability from which a pixel is tree canopy.
Polygons smaller than this many model-input pixels are dropped (400 px is 1 m2 at 0.05 m).
Douglas-Peucker tolerance in model-input pixels; 0 keeps every pixel edge.
